full_judgment:
2. Facts, relevant for disposal of this appeal, in brief, are that, Anil Chandra Sarkar and 6 others had filed Title Suit No. 16 of 2008, against the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Barguna, and 9 others, seeking partition in respect of schedule "Kha" property to the plaint in favour of the plaintiffs stating, inter alia, that, the suit Plot described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint recorded in .RS Khatian Nos. 233, as RS Plot Nos. 224, 225, 226, 227, all these plots subsequently recorded in the SA' Khatian No. 870, comprising 2.42 acres of land, at Mouza Barguan, PS Barguna, District-Bakhergonj, (at present Barguna), were owned and possessed by Ruhini Chandra Sarkar, Kashishar Chandra Sarkar and Ganoranjan Ghosh, that, Ruhini Chandra Sarkar died leaving 4(four) sons, who are plaintiff Nos. 1-4. Kashishar Chandra Sarkar died leaving 2(two) sons, who are plaintiff Nos. 5 and 6 and Ganoranjan Ghosh died leaving only one son, being plaintiff No. 7, that, they have acquired title in the suit property, as heirs of the RS recorded owners. Their further case is that, pursuant to LA Case No. 35/61-62 and LA Case No. 95/63-64, total 97 dEcirnals of land was acquired from RS/ SA Plot No. 224, then 62 decimals of land from SA/RS Plot No. 225, then 41 decimals of land was recorded in RS/SA Plot No. 226 and then 26 decimals of land from RS Plot No. 226 total 2.26 acres of land were acquired in the aforesaid two LA Case No. 35/61-62 and LA Case No. 95/63-64 out of which 1.45 acre were acquired for the TNO office and 81 decimals of land for WAPDA. However, the rest 16 decimals of land were not acquired by the Government. The plaintiffs have claimed their title in this 16 decimals of land as the heirs of SA and R.S recorded owners and prayed for preliminary decree in respect of "Kha" schedule property in their favour. Hence, the plaintiffs had filed this suit with a prayer for partition in respect of the 14 decimals of land (instead of 16 decimals). 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1-3, have contested in the suit by filing written statements, denying title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit property. However, paragraph No. 10 of the written statements they have admitted the fact of acquiring 90 decimals of land from SA Plot No. 224, plus 55 decimals of land from SA Plot No. 225 i.e. total 1.45 acres of land was acquired for Barguna Upzilla Parishad and that in total 2.26 acres of land (including that acquired for WAPDA) acquired by the Government and the same has been recorded in the name of the defendant, vide the Mutation Case No. 1666B/ 2006-2007. Their further case is that, this defendants had acquired 1.45 acres of land for Barguna Upzilla Parishad along with other lands and the total land are lying within their boundary wall and that there was no dispute as regards their title or possession. It has further been stated that, the plaintiff's case is concocted, baseless and they have no legal right or title in the suit property as well as the suit is barred by limitation for filing the same after 45 years of acquisition and that, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The defendant No. 4 has also contested in the suit by filing separate written statement in which he has also stated that, the suit is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed, since the same is barred by limitation and further stating that, total 2.26 acres of land, out of 2.42 acres, were acquired land, lying at SA Plot Nos. 224, 225, 226, 227 of SA Khatian No. 870 and that the defendants were maintaining possession in the rest of the property, since acquisition. 

 7. Learned Advocate Mr. Uzzal Bhowmick with Mr. Tonay Kuar Saha appeared on behalf of the plaintiff-appellants. Mr. Bhowmick, at the very outset submits that, admittedly 2.26 acres of land were acquired out of 2.42 acres, described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint. As such, the rest 16 decimals of and remained un-acquired, which has been described in schedule "Kha" to the plaint. He next submits that, the Government did not claim, nor have been able to show any document in respect of the un-acquired 16 decimals of land. On the other hand, the plaintiffs have clearly stated in paragraph No. 2 of the plaint that they are heirs of RS recorded owners namely, Ruhini Chandra Sarkar, Kashishar Chandra Sarkar and Ganoranjan Ghosh, respectively, and this fact has not been disputed in any way by the defendants. He next submits that, as owner of the suit property described in schedule "Kha" the plaintiff No. 3 Atul Chandra Sarkar submitted an application on 30-1-2008 to the Deputy Commissioner, Barguna, with a prayer to handover the un-acquired 14 decimals of land to them (out of un-acquired 16 decimals). The learned Advocate proceeds on that, the Surveyor of the Upzilla Land Office, in a report dated 21-4-2008 submitted to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), has also admitted that, 14 decimals of land were not acquired, though that were within the boundary wall of the office of the. TNO, Barguna. He has referred to another letter dated 28-4-2008 of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) addressed to the UNO, in which he has also recorded that 14 decimals of land were not acquired and the said property can either been acquired or may be released with the approval of the authority and after demarcation of the same. The learned Advocate then referring to the deposition of PW 1 submits that, the PW 1 has clearly stated that the plaintiffs have submitted the photocopy of the said letters along with the concerned RS and SA Khatian, but the trial court did not mark the photocopies, as Exhibits, although these documents ought to have been marked as exhibits. He empathically argues that, the original of all these documents were lying with the defendants and the photocopies of the same were submitted before the trial court and that the trial ought to have marked those documents as exhibit. The trial court, without taking into consideration these material evidences had passed the impugned judgment and decree, without application of his judicial mind to the law and facts. As regards the question of limitation and the adverse possession claimed for by the defendants, in view of the fact that the suit has been filed after 45 years of the acquisition, the learned Advocate submits that, the Government cannot claim adverse possession in respect of the suit property. In support of his contention he has referred the decision reported in SC 19, 2020(2) SCC 569 (2020) : Vidaya Devi vs The State of Himachal Pradesh in which it has been held that, the state cannot be permitted to perfect its title over the land by invoking the doctrine of adverse possession to grab the property of its own citizen. In conclusion, he submits that, the Government is co-sharer, with the plaintiffs, in schedule "Ka" property and a suit for partition is very much pertinent, but the trial court has utterly failed to appreciate this legal position and wrongly held that, the suit was barred by limitation and has decided the case against the plaintiffs by dismissing the suit and has illegally refused to admit and to consider the aforesaid photocopies as the secondary evidences, which is very much relevant for deciding this case. Hence, he submits that this appeal has merit and the same may kindly be allowed by setting aside the impugned judgment and decree of the trial court, he prays. 

 10. It is not disputed that, the property described in schedule "Ka" to the plaint i.e. RS Khatian No. 233 and SA Khatian No. 870 under Plot Nos. 225, 226 and 227 comprising 2.42 acres of land and that total 2.16 acre of land were acquired in 2 (two) LA Cases Nos. LA Case No. 35/61-62 and LA Case No. 95/63-64, respectively were acquired by the Government. 

 14. We also find that, the PW 1 has clearly stated during his deposition that, they have submitted all these photocopies along with the concerned RS and SA Khatian, but the trial court, although has marked the SA and RS Khatians as exhibited Nos. 1 and 2, however, did not mark the photocopies of these letter, originals of which were lying in the custody of the Government (defendants). Hence, these photocopies docu-ments were admissible as secondary evidence and ought to have been marked as exhibits and taken into consideration as relevant evidence, by the trial court. We, therefore, direct the Bench Officer (BO) of this Court to mark them as exhibits 3 to 5, respectively. 

 16. Besides, from the documentary evidences, as well as the deposition of the PW 1, we find that, the Government is joint owner in the suit property comprising 2.42 acres of land lying in the "Ka" to the plaint i.e. RS Khatian No. 233 and SA Khatian No. 870 under Plot Nos. 225, 226 and 227 comprising 2.42 acres of land and that there remains 16 decimals of land as un-acquired. The Government's title is confined to 2.16 acre, as obtained by acquisition, while the plaintiffs lay their claim for 0.14 (point one four) acre or 14 decimals, as described in schedule "Kha". Therefore, the plaintiffs have prayed to get their share separated through partition and after demarcating the same.
